bounded_statement: Within the supplied files only: the declared independent unit is the mesocosm (mesocosm_id, 12 units, 6 per substrate group), and each mesocosm contributes exactly four repeated outflow samples to data/input.csv. The workflow pools all 48 rows into two groups of 24 and applies scipy.stats.ttest_ind (Welch's two-sample t-test), a procedure whose validity requires each observation to be an independent unit. Each mesocosm therefore enters the row-independent test four times, so the reported statistics (t = -20.228, df = 45.02, p < 1e-06 on 48 'samples') overstate the effective sample size (48 instead of 12) and are not supported by the design. The bounded claim is about the inflated test statistics and degrees of freedom; a correctly aggregated per-mesocosm analysis (n = 6 vs 6 mesocosm means, computable from the report's own per-mesocosm table) would still find a significant difference in the same direction, so the qualitative conclusion of lower zinc under biochar is likely robust even though the quoted inferential quantities are not.

counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow does compute and the report does display per-mesocosm mean zinc values, showing the mesocosm structure was recognized; however, these unit-level means are only tabulated descriptively and are never used in the inferential test.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: Per-mesocosm means tabulated (e.g., MC-01 0.620) but not used in ttest_ind

This limits the practical impact of the flaw but does not negate the procedural issue.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the issue in three ways. (1) I checked whether the workflow aggregates to one value per mesocosm before the test: it does not; mesocosm_values is built but only used for the descriptive table, while group_values pools raw per-row zinc values and those pooled lists are what stats.ttest_ind receives (workflow/analysis.py lines 63-83). (2) I checked whether the procedure used could accommodate clustered/repeated observations: ttest_ind with equal_var=False is a plain Welch two-sample test with no cluster, mixed-effects, or repeated-measures structure, and the report's df = 45.02 confirms all 48 rows were counted as independent observations (a unit-level analysis would have df near 10). (3) I checked whether repeated entries actually occur: data/input.csv contains four rows per mesocosm_id (e.g., MC-01 on lines 2-5) and the report's per-mesocosm table lists 'samples = 4' for all twelve mesocosms, so every independent unit enters the test four times. None of these checks falsified the issue; the only mitigating finding is that a corrected per-mesocosm analysis would still be significant in the same direction, which bounds the impact but does not remove the demonstrated procedural flaw.

root_cause: The analysis code builds group_values by appending the zinc value of every row (every mesocosm-by-week sample) directly into the substrate group's list, then passes those pooled per-row lists to stats.ttest_ind. No aggregation to one value per mesocosm_id is performed before the inferential step, despite the data description designating mesocosm_id as the independent-unit column and stating that treatment was assigned to whole mesocosms and that samples from the same mesocosm share packing, planting, and hydraulic history. Repeated measures from the same independent unit are thus treated as independent replicates (pseudoreplication), inflating n from 12 to 48 and df from ~10 to 45.02.
